# agent.yml sections in detail

All of these are top-level siblings of `agent:`. Unknown keys **under** `fillers`,
`knowledge_answering`, `knowledge_answering.chunking`, and `skill_retrieval` fail
the load; unknown keys under `prompts` are ignored.

## `fillers`

The short line the agent says before a tool call. Every key is optional; an empty or
absent value keeps the built-in default.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | Include the acknowledgement section and reminder. When omitted, on for voice turns and off for text turns. |
| `instructions` | Guidance for acknowledging a tool call in progress. |
| `reminder` | Short reminder injected after the user message on the first model call. |
| `examples` | Few-shot examples, each `{user, ack}`. |

## `prompts`

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `routing_no_active_skill` | Extra routing guidance appended to the catalogue when no skill is active. |

## `knowledge_answering`

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `instructions` | How to write an answer from retrieved knowledge; its own paragraph after the built-in search guidance. A skill's `knowledge_answering.instructions` replaces it while that skill is active. |
| `top_k` | How many chunks a search returns. Default `4`. Read when the trained model loads, so a change needs another train. |
| `embeddings` | Id of a `model_groups` entry used to embed `references/**/*.md`. Empty uses the built-in OpenAI default. Keep the group declared for as long as the trained model is in use. |
| `chunking` | `chunk_size` (default `1000`) and `chunk_overlap` (default `20`), both in **characters**; overlap must be smaller than size. Changing it needs a train, which rebuilds the index. |

Keep `chunk_size` well under the embedder's input limit (8192 tokens for Azure
OpenAI and OpenAI `text-embedding-3-*`). The default stays under it; a much larger
size can fail training.

## `skill_retrieval`

Off unless `active: true`. When it runs, each turn offers only a retrieved subset of
the skills the model can start, instead of the whole catalogue. It is not knowledge
search: `search_knowledge` answers questions from `references/`, while
`skill_retrieval` chooses which skills may be started.

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `active` | `false` | Turn retrieval on. |
| `num_skills` | `20` | Maximum skills returned (at least 1). Retrieval runs only when there are more startable skills than this. |
| `turns_to_embed` | `1` | Recent utterance lines in the search query; `1` is just the current user message. |
| `should_embed_memory` | `true` | Include each skill's memory fields in the index. |
| `embeddings` | empty | Id of a `model_groups` entry; empty uses the built-in default. |

Hidden, disabled, and engine-managed skills are never indexed. Skills with
`always_include_in_prompt: true` and skills started recently in the conversation
stay offered even when search misses them. If search fails while retrieval is
running, the turn fails; there is no fallback to the full list.

## `conversation`

```yaml
conversation:
  before_end:
    - default_customer_satisfaction
```

`before_end` lists skill ids that should complete before the conversation ends.
Voice silence handling is engine-managed (three check-ins, then goodbye and hang up);
its bundled responses can be overridden, but the retry count cannot.

## `voice`

```yaml
voice:
  silence_timeout: 4
```

`silence_timeout` is the seconds to wait after the caller stops speaking (default
`30`, must be greater than `0`). A `silence_timeout` on the voice channel overrides
it. It replaces CALM's `interaction_handling.global_silence_timeout`.

## `tool_timeout`

Seconds, default `10`. Applies to local `@tool` functions, and to imported MCP tools
when their server sets no `tool_timeout` of its own. On timeout the call is
cancelled and an error goes back to the model. Raise it for slow backends.

## `session_config`

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `session_expiration_time` | `60` | Session lifetime in minutes; `0` disables expiry, a negative value fails validation. |
| `start_session_after_expiry` | `true` | Start a new session on the next message after expiry. |

## `privacy`

Accepts only `tracker_store_settings` (anonymization and deletion cron jobs). A
`rules` list is rejected: per-field anonymization belongs on memory fields with
`pii: true`.

## `orchestrator.tool_constraints`

Tunes the built-in framework tools. Omitting a tool keeps its default offer rules.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` removes the tool. Allowed on `cancel`, `complete`, `search_knowledge`, and `cannot_help` only. |
| `invoke_when` | Replaces the prompt lines that say when to call the tool. Blank text fails validation. |
| `requires_confirmation` | On `cancel` only: `enabled: true` pauses cancel until the user confirms, with optional `utter_for_confirmation` / `utter_on_user_denial` response names. |

`activate`, `correct`, and `set_fields` reject `enabled: false`. `listen`, `hangup`,
`resolve_tool_confirmation`, and unknown names fail validation. When cancel
confirmation is on, don't also tell the model to ask before cancelling; that asks
twice. Turn `complete` off only when every skill finishes without the orchestrator.
